name: Charles Buckey McKeldin
notable_stories: Maintained a lifelong family feud with his brothers-in-law over an insurance policy payout after his first wife's death
Lifelong falling-out with brothers-in-law (Kenneth and George Schriefer Jr.) over Emily's insurance policy payout after her 1950 death (memoir p. 13-14)

CORRECTION: Family lore of 'four sisters Lola/Lillian/Helen/Emma + brother Billy' as Buckey's siblings likely refers to his AUNTS AND UNCLES (Charles E McKeldin I's siblings), not Buckey's own siblings. Buckey had siblings from his mother Emma Bell McKeldin — these are yet to be confirmed from records.
His sisters called him 'Buckey'. His wife (Barbara's stepmother Peggy) hated the nickname and once said on the drive home from a visit that she would be sick if she heard 'Buckey' one more time.

He took the children to Orioles and Colts games, the Ringling Brothers circus and Barbara's Saturday duckpin bowling, and took them fishing on the Chesapeake Bay at Ocean City. Sunday country drives ended with ice cream if they behaved.
Brian and Brendan called him Pops (with Peggy as Granny).
Buckey and Peggy visited the Adamses out west every other year, came for both boys' First Communions, and stayed at their Kelso house for Mike and Shelley's wedding.
The family called him 'Pops', and he and Peggy were 'Granny and Pops' to the grandchildren.

He went to the Duck Carvers Convention in Ocean City and always came back with bird pins or decoys; he carved a few himself, including a swan and a Santa, and at his death Barbara split his decoys with her brothers.
With Peggy he went on the 1993 Alaska cruise with Barbara and John, and on a Hawaii trip with them and Nana that took in Oahu, Maui and the Big Island.
His favourite tree was the dogwood, and he gave Barbara a pinkie ring engraved with her initials BJM.
milestones: Raised children Barbara and Chuck in Baltimore
Became a patriarch for his expanded family
Married Margaret Frances Peggy Quinn (wife 2; b. 12 Mar 1927, d. 18 Nov 2008)

Religion: He was not Catholic but went to church with his mother every Sunday, prayed kneeling by his bed every night, and paid for his children to go to Catholic school. He became Catholic while Barbara was in college. (about 1966-1969)
sources: Barbara McKeldin Adams, "Barbara McKeldin Adams - A Memoir" (privately printed)
notes: Father of Barbara Jeanne Adams, Chuck McKeldin, and J. Michael McKeldin
Siblings listed: Sisters Lola, Lillian, Helen, and Emma

CORRECTION 2026-09-23: Lola, Lillian, Helen, Emma and William "Billy" are his sisters and brother, as his daughter Barbara states twice in her memoir, not Charles E. McKeldin I's siblings as an earlier note suggested. (Charles E. I also had a sister Lillian and a brother William, which likely caused the mix-up.) [Barbara McKeldin Adams, A Memoir, text line 392, 4153]
Barbara lists "Edward, after my father" among possible names for her son Brian, which suggests the E. in his name stood for Edward (not confirmed). [Barbara McKeldin Adams, A Memoir, text line 1591]
His Find a Grave memorial names him Charles Edward McKeldin (1917–2006), confirming that the E. stood for Edward.
